findings.claim: The front-seam warrant's own contrast is not byte-supported: the 'second-person address' versus 'first-person-plural admission' opposition fails because the second half of the same verse opens on second-person address too, and first-person-plural verbs already stand in the preceding panel.
findings.grounds: oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5 opens its second half on הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier), second-person address identical in person to the first half's פָּגַ֤עְתָּ ... בִּדְרָכֶ֖יךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier); the only genuinely new element is the first-person-plural verb וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier). First-person-plural verbs already stand in the preceding panel at הָיִ֗ינוּ (oshb:Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19, the split verse's first half, byte tier) and נְקַוֶּ֑ה (oshb:Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3, byte tier). The row's underlying fact re-verifies -- no confession-of-sin verb stands anywhere in oshb:Isa.63.15-Isa.64.3 -- so the seam itself survives; only the stated contrast is defective.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: re-cut the contrast to rest on the first-person-plural confession verb alone (spliced at oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5) and drop the person-shift framing, which the same verse's own bytes contradict.

findings.claim: The rear-seam hinge device -- 'a final unanswered double question', carried into observed_substrate_signals as speech_formula.unanswered_closing_question -- is established only from the WEB rendering's two question marks; the row carries no Hebrew splice or accent citation at its own closing verse, where a single interrogative particle governs both clauses across the caesura.
findings.grounds: oshb:Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12 reads הַעַל אֵ֥לֶּה תִתְאַפַּ֖ק יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier) / תֶּחֱשֶׁ֥ה וּתְעַנֵּ֖נוּ עַד מְאֹֽד (byte tier): ONE interrogative he, on the first token, with the atnach on the fourth token; the second clause carries no interrogative particle of its own. The row's only citation for the 'double question' is the curly-quoted WEB run at web:Isa.64.12, which re-checks verbatim but is a tier-4 translation-punctuation fact. The answering divine reply that carries the same seam is likewise asserted at oshb:Isa.65.1 with no Hebrew splice anywhere in the row.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: splice the interrogative particle and the atnach position at oshb:Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12 and re-ground the closure device in the Hebrew, or re-label the observed_substrate_signals key so it does not rest on the translation's sentence punctuation.

findings.claim: frontier_flag_considered is false while the row's own device_notes calls the confession onset 'a soft, tonal seam rather than a formal header', and the book-order neighbour that owns the other side of the identical seam flags that same ground as a genuine frontier question.
findings.grounds: This row (span Isa.64.5-Isa.64.12) sets frontier_flag_considered false; the previous row (span Isa.63.15-Isa.64.4) sets it true and states the ground as the seam separating petition-recollection from confession being argued from a rhetorical-mode shift rather than a formal header. Both rows argue the same web:Isa.64.4 | web:Isa.64.5 (= oshb:Isa.64.3 | oshb:Isa.64.4) seam, from the same ground, at the same medium_low confidence. No formal signal stands at the seam: oshb:Isa.64.4 opens on the verb פָּגַ֤עְתָּ (byte tier) with no vocative, messenger frame, speaker change or addressee change from oshb:Isa.64.3, and the paragraph-mark inventory records no petuchah or setumah at MT 64:3 (single-witness; absence not counterevidence).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: set frontier_flag_considered true, matching both the neighbour row and this row's own stated ground.

findings.claim: Workflow register in row prose: the rejected alternative narrates the campaign's own disclosure obligation instead of stating the rival.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative reads 'since a mandated rival reading treats 64:4's ... as already confessional in tone'. 'Mandated' names a process obligation, not a textual fact; no other row in the batch narrates the obligation.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: delete 'mandated' and state the rival reading directly.

findings.claim: The mid-verse position digit's denominator is a staged-token count inflated by the ketiv/qere doubling in the very verse the row cites for its K/Q note; the verse carries 18 word slots, staged as 19 tokens.
findings.grounds: oshb:Isa.65.7 stages the K/Q pair as two adjacent tokens, על אֶל (tokens 17-18 of 19, byte tier); the disclosure inventory records exactly one K/Q note at MT 65:7 (single-witness). The cited position itself re-verifies exactly: אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier) stands at tokens 5-6, before אֲשֶׁ֤ר קִטְּרוּ֙ (tokens 7-8, byte tier) and before חֵרְפ֑וּנִי (token 13) and וּמַדֹּתִ֧י (token 14), byte tier. Only the denominator's count object is undisclosed; the position claim and the K/Q disclosure are sound.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: name the count object -- '19 staged tokens, the K/Q pair staged as two' -- or state the position against the 18 word slots.

findings.claim: The cross-seam tie carries a byte-false position claim: the former-things noun does not open the next verse, and the row's own next clause names the token that does.
findings.grounds: oshb:Isa.65.17's first token is כִּֽי (byte tier); הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (byte tier) stands at token 10 of 14. At oshb:Isa.65.16 the same pointed form הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת (byte tier) stands at token 15 of 18, whose final token is מֵעֵינָֽי (byte tier), so 'closing this unit' is a loose position claim as well. The byte-identity and the digit both re-verify: a sweep at that pointed form returns 2 verses book-wide at BYTE tier (MT 65:16, 65:17), against 3 verses accent-stripped and 5 skeleton -- the row's 'pointed form' qualifier is doing real work and is correctly stated.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: replace 'closing this unit' / 'opening the next verse' with position-neutral wording (the same pointed form standing in both verses), or state the true token positions.

findings.claim: 'my servants' blessing is embedded throughout' overstates the span: the my-servants token stands in two of the row's four verses, and the third servant token in the span is a different referent object.
findings.grounds: The my-servants form עֲבָדַ֤י (oshb:Isa.65.13, byte tier) stands 3x in that verse and עֲבָדַ֛י (oshb:Isa.65.14, byte tier) once in the next; those are the only two verses of the span carrying it. The servant token at the third verse is instead the third-masculine-singular-suffixed וְלַעֲבָדָ֥יו (oshb:Isa.65.15, byte tier), a different referent object, and oshb:Isa.65.16 carries no servant token at any tier. The row's own adjacent digit ('sweep: 2 verses') states the true extent.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: narrow 'throughout' to the span's first two verses and name the count object separating the my-servants form from the his-servants form.

findings.claim: The rejected alternative's ground -- that 66:1-2 and 66:3-4 remain inside one frame 'with no intervening tier-1 seam' -- is not byte-true as stated: an undisclosed divine-speech signature stands inside the span, at the caesura of the row's second verse.
findings.grounds: oshb:Isa.66.2 carries נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier) at tokens 9-10 of 20, standing on the verse's atnach; the same formula's book-wide census is 23 verses (verse count, skeleton tier), and the corpus treats it as a closure signal elsewhere in this same chapter. The shipped span nonetheless survives: the signature is mid-verse and oshb:Isa.66.2 continues past it with וְאֶל זֶ֣ה אַבִּ֔יט (byte tier) inside the same declaration, so it closes no verse. But neither boundary_rationale nor device_notes discloses it, while oshb:Isa.66.2 is already cited in boundary_evidence_refs for other content. All other checks on this row pass: the koh-amar onset, the catchword pair and the 7-verse trembling-root sweep (skeleton tier) re-verify exactly, and both bracketing SAMEKH marks match the inventory at MT 65:25 and MT 66:4 under the claimed type.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: disclose the mid-verse divine-speech signature at oshb:Isa.66.2 and restate the rejection ground as positioned (no seam-eligible verse-final signal) rather than absolute.

findings.claim: The 5-verse digit is bound to the wrong count object: the three-word herald phrase the sentence names is a book-wide hapax, and 5 is the count for the bare one-word verse-initial opener.
findings.grounds: ק֤וֹל שָׁאוֹן֙ מֵעִ֔יר (oshb:Isa.66.6, byte tier) returns 1 verse book-wide at byte, accent-stripped AND skeleton tiers. The bare verse-initial one-word opener ק֤וֹל (oshb:Isa.66.6, byte tier) returns 5 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (MT 13:4, 40:3, 40:6, 52:8, 66:6). The row quotes the three-word phrase and then attaches '(sweep: 5 verses book-wide at that verse-initial opener, skeleton tier)' to it, so the digit's stated object and its true object differ.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: name the swept object explicitly (the one-word verse-initial herald opener, skeleton tier, 5 verses) and keep the three-word phrase as the byte-tier splice with no digit attached.

findings.claim: Confidence 'high' with frontier_flag_considered false does not survive the row's own stated grounds, which concede a live verse-initial tier-1 rival inside the span and then override it on content alone.
findings.grounds: The row's strongest_rejected_alternative states in terms that the internal split is rejected 'not on the ground that no tier-1 signal divides them', names a verse-initial herald-voice formula at oshb:Isa.66.6, and names a second-person-to-third-person shift from oshb:Isa.66.5 -- then rests the rejection on content. Sibling rows in this part carry frontier_flag_considered true for softer, purely thematic tensions with no conceded tier-1 rival. No respan is proposed: the mark layer independently brackets the shipped span with SAMEKH at MT 66:4 and MT 66:9 (single-witness, tier-3, not drivers), and the content ground is reasonable.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: set frontier_flag_considered true and reduce confidence from high to medium, matching the row's own conceded rival.

findings.claim: The verse-final accent clause is not supportable from the staged bytes: the cited final token does carry a mark at the silluq position, and every verse-final token in the extract carries the same mark, so the claim is either false or vacuous.
findings.grounds: The final token of oshb:Isa.66.9 is אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (byte tier); its codepoints include U+05BD after the qamats -- the silluq position. The same U+05BD stands on the final token of oshb:Isa.65.16 (מֵעֵינָֽי), oshb:Isa.65.25 (יְהוָֽה) and oshb:Isa.66.14 (אֹיְבָֽיו), byte tier. Verse-final tokens in this extract bear no U+0591-U+05AF cantillation accent as a class, so 'its final token carrying no dividing accent' distinguishes nothing and is false if the silluq is counted. The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so the clause is also not machine-checkable as written.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: drop the accent clause, or restate it as 'no U+0591-U+05AF cantillation accent, the silluq standing as on every verse-final token'.

findings.claim: The rear seam's sole stated warrant is undercut by an undisclosed verse-initial subordinating connector: the verse the row calls 'the first formally marked onset of the judgment unit' opens on that connector, binding it to the row's own closing verse.
findings.grounds: oshb:Isa.66.15's first token is כִּֽי (byte tier), opening כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ (byte tier). The row's device_notes states that, no mark falling at oshb:Isa.66.14, the 66:14 | 66:15 seam 'rests on the tier-1 theophany-onset signal alone' -- the paragraph-mark inventory does confirm no petuchah or setumah at MT 66:14 (single-witness; absence not counterevidence) -- yet neither boundary_rationale nor device_notes discloses the connector. Sibling rows in this same part disclose the identical construction at oshb:Isa.65.17 (כִּֽי, byte tier) as an unmarked continuity the subject-and-register shift is argued against rather than around. Every other claim in this row re-verifies: the koh-amar splice at oshb:Isa.66.12, all four WEB runs verbatim, the front-seam SAMEKH at MT 66:11 and the paseq at MT 66:12 (count-only, no position asserted).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: disclose the verse-initial subordinating connector at oshb:Isa.66.15 as unmarked cross-seam continuity that the register shift is argued against, matching the sibling rows' treatment of the same construction.
